reader.requirement: At --std 85 a data description entry with OCCURS ... DEPENDING ON must be followed, within its record description (file, working-storage or linkage), only by entries subordinate to it: any later non-subordinate entry at the same or a higher level, however deeply the table is nested, must be refused, while subordinate entries (and the start of a new record) are accepted.

reader.notes: OdoResolvePass climbs from the table to its record and refuses any later non-REDEFINES sibling at each level (COBOL0856). The REDEFINES exemption is narrower than the 1985 words but no legal 1985 source reaches it: probe o1b is refused by the REDEFINES placement rule. Level-66 entries follow the record description (§1985:VI.5.11.3 SR2) and were not treated as part of it.

refuter.evidence: cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.8.3 SR10 (the text is in SR10); OK  §1985:VI.5.10.3 SR5 (the text is in SR5). I attacked the REDEFINES exemption in OdoResolvePass's following-entry climb: r5a.cob (05 G1 holding the ODO table, then 05 G2 REDEFINES G1) is refused COBOL0855 (an ODO table within a REDEFINES area, which §1985:VI.5.10.3 SR5 forbids), so the skipped follower is still refused. r5c.cob (SD record: ODO followed by sibling SZ) is refused COBOL0856; r5d.cob (CD record in the Communication Section: ODO followed by CZ) is refused COBOL0856; r5b.cob (66 RENAMES after a record whose last entry is an ODO table) is accepted and prints [3Q], which is right because RENAMES entries follow the record description and are not in it.
